![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14233881/assets/f940a05c937b3158ce737959dee4685d216e6d55d6651672aa910cdb2c492f1e.png)

The scatter plot for the data sets $x$ and $y$ of paired observations and the corresponding linear regression line are shown above.

According to the regression model, what is the residual for the highlighted datapoint?
question.worked_solution:
The residual equals the difference between the actual value of the dependent variable and the value estimated using the linear regression model:

$$
\text{Residual}=\text{Actual}-\text{Estimated}
$$

 

The highlighted datapoint has coordinates $(5,1).$ So, our actual value is $y=1.$

On the other hand, the point on the regression line that corresponds to $x=5$ has the $y$-coordinate $0.$ So, our estimated value of is $\overset{^}{y}=0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14233881/assets/937c0307a74881c87e6a33c47b32a1ac2d5124326b13538455640cd9fc88c14e.png)

Therefore, the residual is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Residual} & =\text{Actual}-\text{Estimated} \\  & =y-\overset{^}{y} \\  & =1-0 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
